question: Does one standalone 128K-capable model execute the qualified native layer loop and reproduce all previous language, deduction and full-history results?
protocol: Freeze every existing component. Fit an input-only binary selector using all 1536 training induction prompts against 240 training deduction examples and the existing selector's 384 mixed training prompts. Use full-batch Adam .003, 160 updates, confidence .99. Export to standalone MLX, independently reload its runtime and both readers, then run the entire qualification from the exported weights. Replay all 64 native confirmation requests at 768 tokens, all 56 deduction requests at 768, all 80 registered mixed turns at their original caps, all 120 raw passages and two real 131083-input-token resident full-history key swaps. Timing includes routing, encoding, full prefill and free greedy generation.
gate: Stop on first unequal output token or change to a reference route, any difference in raw language NLL, memory warning or budget exhaustion. Require both 128K counterfactuals correct with the annotated gold in the selected span and total long-context time <=1.75x exact prior Base, a verified standalone export and all 200 previous short responses identical.
